The act is jure imperii: a killing carried out by a minister in the exercise of state power is a sovereign act, not a commercial one, so it cannot be jure gestionis. The territorial tort exception to state immunity (UN Convention on Jurisdictional Immunities, Art. 12) covers only acts occurring in the forum state, so a killing committed abroad falls outside it, and the ICJ in *Germany v. Italy* (2012) held that jus cogens violations do not remove state immunity.
